name: Minimum-variance portfolio (two assets)
use: The lowest-risk combination of two stocks.

name: Risk-free mix when ρ = −1
pitfall: Special case ρ = 0: x_1 = σ_2² / (σ_1² + σ_2²).

name: Mixing with the risk-free asset (CAL)
use: Lending (0 < x < 1) or borrowing (x > 1) combined with a risky portfolio P.

vars.meaning: expected return and volatility of the combination
fraction of own money in P; 1 − x goes into the risk-free asset
expected return and volatility of the risky portfolio P

pitfall: Leverage scales premium and risk in the same proportion – the Sharpe ratio stays.

name: Sharpe ratio
use: Ranking risky portfolios when you can borrow and lend at r_f.

vars.meaning: Sharpe ratio of portfolio P (excess return per unit of risk)

pitfall: Positive Sharpe = beats r_f in expectation; it says nothing about 'above one'.

name: Hitting a target risk or return
formula: \begin{aligned} \text{target risk:}\quad x &= \dfrac{\sigma_{\text{target}}}{\sigma_T} \\[8pt] \text{target return:}\quad x &= \dfrac{E_{\text{target}} - r_f}{E(R_T) - r_f} \end{aligned}
use: Beat a given portfolio with the tangency (or market) portfolio.

vars.meaning: weight in the tangency portfolio T (x > 1 = borrowing)
volatility / expected return you want to reach
